about: Golden vectors for canonicalization and hashing of Ductus evidence v2 (DAN-127). All data is invented.
The file is ASCII: every non-ASCII character is written as a \u escape. Read it with a JSON parser from the file bytes, not through a bundler import, which may rewrite keys such as __proto__.

The expected values were derived outside the repository (RFC texts, hand-written canonical strings, an independent implementation). Never regenerate them from the code under test: a change that alters any value is a change of the evidence contract.

definitions.canonicalBytes: UTF-8 encoding of the RFC 8785 (JCS) serialization of a JSON value. No Unicode normalization. A lone surrogate or a non-finite number has no canonical form.
definitions.documentHash: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the canonical bytes of the canonical document JSON.
definitions.segmentHash: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the canonical bytes of an evidence segment v2. The server hashes the bytes it received and accepts them only when they are the canonical bytes of a valid segment.
definitions.chain: predecessorSegmentHash is the segmentHash of the segment accepted before it, null for the first. The head is the last segmentHash together with the number of segments.
definitions.segmentTime: observedStartedAt and observedEndedAt are whole minutes in UTC, written YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:00.000Z. An event has no time; events are ordered by sequence. Nothing else in a segment carries time.
definitions.receiptDigest: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the canonical bytes of the receipt payload v1 (payloadDigestSha256).
definitions.receiptSignatureV1: Ed25519 (RFC 8032, pure) over the canonical bytes of the receipt payload v1; raw 64-byte signature, base64url without padding. Decision D-92 replaces this for receipt v2.

documents.name: editor-like-document
documents.note: An invented document in an editor-like JSON shape. The vector fixes the JCS form and the hash of this JSON value only; how the editor serializes its model is not defined here.

chain.note: Two chained segments from the empty document to a signed receipt for each. Steps use an invented test format: insert-text at a UTF-16 offset of the text of one node. Receipts are signed with the Ed25519 test key published as TEST 1 in RFC 8032 section 7.1; only its public half is stored here. signingSeedSha256 is the SHA-256 of the 32 private bytes printed in the RFC, so that a test can show those bytes are in none of the vector files.

segmentPayloads.note: Byte edits of chain.segments[base].canonicalUtf8Hex that must not be accepted. find/replace are UTF-8 text, findHex/replaceHex are bytes; find occurs exactly once. recanonicalizesToBase: the edited bytes parse to the same segment, so only the bytes are wrong. canonicalJcs: the edited bytes are canonical JCS, so the segment validator is what rejects them.

eventTime.note: Owner decision of 10 October 2026 (D-24, D-56): a segment carries no time per event and no time finer than a minute, and the server refuses a segment that does; it never rounds one. formerSegments are the two chain segments of the first revision of this file (DAN-127), byte for byte: canonical JCS that was valid then and must be refused now, because its events carry occurredAt and elapsedMs and its observed times carry seconds. formerSegmentHash is the hash that revision published for them. The edits with the classes event-time, time-precision, time-form, time-in-identifier, time-in-step and closed-shape under segmentPayloads.rejected each break one rule on the current first segment.

identifiers.note: documentId, sessionId, segmentId and every touched node id are refused when they have a layout that embeds the time of creation: a UUID of version 1, 6 or 7, or a ULID, in either letter case. This names known layouts only; it does not make any other identifier free of time, and it prescribes no layout.

sizeLimit.note: Set events[0].steps[0].text of segmentWithoutPadding to padding.unit repeated padding.count times. The unit is two UTF-8 bytes and one UTF-16 code unit, so the limit is seen to count bytes. The document hashes in the segment are those of the padded document. overLimit appends extraText to that text.
